companies.name: Amwaste LLC
companies.subsector: Solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling
companies.description: Amwaste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling services in the Southeastern United States. Its customer base includes residential, commercial, construction and industrial end markets across Alabama, Georgia, and Louisiana. The business operates an asset-heavy, vertically integrated model supported by owned disposal sites, transfer stations, and recycling infrastructure. Public materials describe a platform with more than 300,000 customers, eight landfill sites, ten transfer stations, and a materials recovery facility. The company has expanded through bolt-on acquisitions and local contract wins to deepen density in its core Southeastern markets. 3i invested growth capital through the 3i North American Infrastructure Fund in July 2023, and current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

companies.description: EC Waste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, recycling, and disposal services across Puerto Rico. companies.name: Regional Rail, LLC
companies.description: Regional Rail owns and operates short-line freight railroads and related rail services across the United States and Canada. Its customer base spans industrial, agricultural, chemicals, aggregates, food, and logistics end markets that depend on local freight connectivity and transload services. The company follows an asset-heavy operating model built around owned and leased track, rail-served industrial infrastructure, and operating railroad franchises. Public disclosures describe a network of more than 875 route miles, 17 railroad operations, and approximately 65,000 annual carloads as of 2023. The footprint expanded materially after 2019 through acquisitions in Florida, the Midwest, Ohio, Indiana, and western Canada. 3i invested in Regional Rail in July 2019 as its North American rail infrastructure platform and remains the disclosed owner.

companies.name: JVR Energy Park
companies.description: JVR Energy Park is a co-located solar and battery storage project in southeastern San Diego County. Its customer base is San Diego Community Power and the California grid, which will receive contracted renewable energy and storage capacity from the project. The project follows an asset-heavy contracted operating model based on utility-scale generation and storage infrastructure. Public disclosures describe a 90 megawatt AC solar facility paired with a 70 megawatt AC and 280 megawatt-hour battery storage system, with expected output sufficient to serve about 57,000 homes. BayWa r.e. developed the project and closed full financing in 2025 as it advanced toward commercial operations in 2026. Acadia participated through preferred equity in the 2025 financing package, while BayWa r.e. remains the disclosed project sponsor and developer.

companies.name: Peregrine Energy Storage Project
companies.description: Peregrine is a utility-scale battery storage facility in the Barrio Logan area of San Diego. Its customer base is the California power system, where the project provides energy shifting, capacity, and grid-reliability services rather than retail electricity supply. The facility follows an asset-heavy storage-infrastructure model centered on a standalone battery project connected to the local transmission system. Public disclosures describe a 200 megawatt and 400 megawatt-hour lithium-ion battery system that became Arevon's fifth operating utility-scale storage facility in California. The project reached commercial operation in 2025 after Arevon closed a project financing package that included debt, tax equity, and preferred equity components. Acadia's role was publicly described as sourcing preferred equity for the financing, while Arevon remained the disclosed developer, owner, and operator.

companies.name: Astoria Project Partners Holdings LLC
companies.description: Astoria Energy comprises two adjacent combined-cycle gas-fired generation facilities in Queens that supply dispatchable power to the New York City market. Its customers are wholesale power-market participants and, in the case of Astoria Energy II, the New York Power Authority under a long-term tolling arrangement. The assets operate under a mixed model in which Astoria Energy I sells output on a merchant basis into NYISO while Astoria Energy II benefits from contracted revenues. Public disclosures describe the two facilities at a combined roughly 1.2 gigawatts of capacity and position them as important sources of reliable power in New York City. The plants are asset-heavy thermal generation infrastructure located in Astoria, one of the densest load pockets in the United States. An APG-led consortium agreed to acquire 100% of Astoria Energy I and 55% of Astoria Energy II in January 2020 and closed the transaction in July 2020.

companies.description: Cross-Sound Cable owns and operates a high-voltage direct-current submarine transmission link between Connecticut and Long Island. The full corridor opened ahead of schedule in November 2022. Ferrovial's audited 2025 filing reports Cintra at 55.7%, Meridiam Infrastructure S.a.r.l. at 29.75%, and I-66 Blocker (APG) at 14.55%.

companies.name: Arthur Kill Terminal
companies.description: Arthur Kill Terminal is a heavy-lift marine terminal project under development on Staten Island, New York for offshore wind staging and assembly. The facility is intended to serve offshore wind developers and marine logistics users through an asset-heavy port infrastructure model rather than a traditional shipping terminal concession. Public project materials describe a roughly 32.5-acre site with marine improvements designed to handle large turbine components. Apollo-managed funds announced in 2021 that they had secured the exclusive right to invest in the project alongside Atlantic Offshore Terminals, but reviewed public materials do not disclose the current finalized ownership structure. The project continued through permitting and development work, although a previously awarded federal port grant was later withdrawn in 2025.

companies.name: Broad Reach Power
companies.description: Broad Reach Power was a Houston-based utility-scale battery storage and renewable-energy platform founded by EnCap Energy Transition in 2019. Apollo-managed infrastructure funds collectively acquired a 50% stake in December 2021 alongside the EnCap-led shareholder group. Apollo confirms that Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II participated, but its individual allocation was not publicly disclosed. EnCap and Apollo announced the sale of Broad Reach Power's battery-storage business to ENGIE in August 2023, excluding 1.8 GW of solar and wind projects and 4 GWh of Mountain West battery projects from the transaction perimeter. ENGIE finalized its acquisition of 100% of Broad Reach Power from EnCap and Apollo in October 2023 and fully consolidated the acquired business. ENGIE's audited 2025 financial statements continue to report 100% ownership of Group Broad Reach Power, while EnCap classifies Broad Reach Power as realized in 2023. No current Apollo ownership or subsequent reacquisition was found through August 8, 2026. Public sources reviewed do not disclose the post-closing ownership or operating identity of the excluded Mountain West portfolio.

companies.description: LAZ Parking provides parking management, valet, shuttle, enforcement, and related mobility services for airports, municipalities, hospitals, universities, and commercial real estate owners. NGPL provides firm, flexible-firm and interruptible transportation, multiple storage products, balancing, park-and-loan and line-pack services. ArcLight-controlled funds own 62.5%, comprising a 37.5% Fund VII interest and a separate 25% investment whose fund and vehicle split is not publicly disclosed, while Kinder Morgan owns 37.5% and operates the system. companies.name: Indian Energy
companies.description: Archived PortCo-census record for Indian Energy, LLC, an active Native American-owned developer, integrator, owner and operator of resilient microgrids, renewable generation and energy storage. Indian Energy is a qualifying infrastructure operating company, but no direct BlackRock or GIP equity ownership was established. The relationship previously recorded as a BlackRock GEPIF III ownership period was instead an approximately US$25 million BlackRock Impact Opportunities bridge loan supporting the Viejas Enterprise Microgrid project. Indian Energy identified BlackRock Impact Opportunities as a financing partner at the September 2024 project financial close, and a direct 2026 BlackRock Impact Opportunities interview said the bridge capital had earned a return and been returned. A July 2024 tribal-government resolution separately disclosed a 15% direct Indian Energy interest held by the Sault Ste. Marie Tribe. The complete current cap table is not public, but the evidence is sufficient to exclude the company from the requested BlackRock and GIP PortCo lists. The record is archived rather than represented as a realized infrastructure-fund equity investment.

The former owners' 61.7% and 38.3% direct interests ended at closing. PNGTS maintains a corporate office in Houston and an operating office in Lancaster, New Hampshire. No later company sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

companies.name: Hill Top Energy Center
companies.description: Hill Top Energy Center is a 620 MW natural-gas combined-cycle power plant in Carmichaels, Pennsylvania that sells energy and capacity into PJM. The FERC record identifies 76.28% and 14.72% aggregator interests for those two vehicles; the internal allocation of the remaining 9% among other affiliated vehicles is not publicly disclosed. The plant company is the canonical PortCo, while buyer and seller holding entities are not counted separately. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

companies.name: Rover Pipeline
companies.description: Rover Pipeline LLC is a large-scale interstate natural gas transmission system connecting Marcellus and Utica production in Pennsylvania and West Virginia with demand markets across Ohio, Michigan and the broader Midwest. CIM remains the current manager-level sponsor of Novva; its fund, vehicle and ownership percentage are not public. 400 Paul is an underlying facility and alias rather than a separate PortCo. companies.description: Permanent Power Company is a CIM Group-backed U.S. power-infrastructure platform that owns and develops utility-scale solar generation, battery storage and transmission assets. At March 31, 2026, CIM Opportunity Zone Fund held approximately 66.7% of the company, including its direct interest and the interest held through COZ 1, while other CIM-affiliated entities held the remaining 33.3%. Westlands Solar Park is the California site/master plan beneath Permanent Power, and Aquamarine is its first 250 MW utility-scale solar project rather than a separate portfolio company. The Westlands development lineage began in 2014, construction started in 2020 and Aquamarine entered commercial operation in late 2021. The exact rename effective date, company headquarters and identities within the 33.3% CIM-affiliate block are not publicly disclosed. No third-party sale, change of control or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

companies.description: Vineyard Offshore is Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' U.S. offshore-wind development platform, established in 2022 with federal lease interests held through CI IV. Vineyard Northeast, Vineyard Wind 2, Excelsior Wind and their lease SPVs are consolidated beneath this one platform record; Vineyard Wind 1 remains distinct.

companies.description: WideOpenWest, Inc. (WOW!) is a U.S. broadband network operator providing high-speed internet, video, voice, mobile, business data and related connectivity services to residential, commercial and wholesale customers. The company operates across 19 markets in Michigan, Alabama, Tennessee, South Carolina, Georgia and Florida and reports nearly two million network passings. Operations began in 2001; the current corporation was formed in 2012 and adopted the WideOpenWest name in 2017. Crestview first invested in December 2015. InfraBridge is not a direct owner. SoftBank's signed acquisition of DigitalBridge remains an upstream manager transaction and was not treated as a direct WOW ownership transfer through August 19, 2026.

companies.description: Anza Renewables is the operating brand of Anza RE, LLC, a U.S. software-enabled procurement, data and analytics platform serving solar and battery-storage developers, independent power producers and other energy buyers. The company is headquartered in Oakland, California and reports more than 80 subscribers and support for over 8 GW of PV and 5 GWh of BESS purchase orders. companies.description: Gopher Resource is the operating name of Gopher Resource, LLC, a U.S. lead-battery recycling platform founded in 1946 and headquartered in Eagan, Minnesota. A 2025 federal disclosure identifies ECP Gopher Holdings, LP as the sole immediate parent; the ECP economic interest, purchase price, rollover and co-investors are not publicly disclosed. EnviroFocus, Resource Plastics, the facilities and The Recycling Zone remain subsidiaries, assets or operated sites rather than separate PortCos. A 2020 internal ECP HSR notice and the October 2024 US$450 million refinancing do not establish an outside-party exit, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

companies.description: Reworld is a North American waste-to-energy and resource recovery platform. companies.name: Rio Grande LNG
companies.description: Rio Grande LNG is a large-scale LNG liquefaction and export terminal under construction at the Port of Brownsville, Texas. Phase 1 closed on July 12, 2023 with equity from Global Infrastructure Partners, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade. The same investor group participated in later Train 4 and Train 5 transactions through separate project vehicles. XRG subsequently acquired partial GIP interests: 11.7% of Phase 1 and 7.6% across Trains 4 and 5. GIP remains an active investor after those partial sell-downs. BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP did not create a separate Rio Grande LNG ownership period. At June 2026, Trains 1 and 2 were 74.0% complete, Train 3 was 50.4%, Train 4 was 15.5% and Train 5 was 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027. Train and holding entities are treated as project vehicles beneath the one terminal record. No signed pending company-level exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

companies.name: Zenith Energy Portland Terminal
companies.description: Zenith Energy Portland Terminal is a standalone liquid-bulk storage and multimodal fuels terminal at 5501 NW Front Avenue on Portland's Willamette River. Its customer base includes refiners, marketers, traders, and other energy counterparties that use the system for storage, transportation, blending, and related logistics services. The operating model is asset-heavy and infrastructure-based because cash flows are tied to pipeline transportation, terminal throughput, storage, and marine-services activity. Public company and sponsor materials describe more than 5,000 miles of domestic pipeline, more than 130 liquid-petroleum terminals, and approximately 125 million barrels of tank capacity across key U.S. and international markets. IFM Global Infrastructure Fund agreed to acquire Buckeye in 2019 and completed the take-private in November 2019; the current ownership split among IFM-advised vehicles is not publicly disclosed. Buckeye remains one of IFM’s largest North American midstream holdings.

companies.description: Altius Renewable Royalties acquires and manages royalty interests tied to wind, solar, and other renewable energy projects. Its customers are effectively renewable project owners and developers that monetize a portion of future project revenues in exchange for growth capital, making the model contractual and asset-light rather than owner-operator based. companies.name: Bandwidth Infrastructure Group, LLC d/b/a BIG Fiber
companies.description: BIG Fiber builds and operates metro dark fiber networks for data centers, hyperscalers, and enterprise customers. Bandwidth IG rebranded to BIG Fiber in 2025 as it continued to expand its dark fiber platform.

companies.description: Intermountain Infrastructure Group, LLC develops, owns and operates long-haul and regional fiber networks, offering dark fiber, wavelengths, high-capacity internet and colocation. The U.S.-headquartered platform is building and operating routes across the western and northern United States, with Canada as a secondary market. Its Northern Tier system is a wholly owned multi-conduit route designed to connect the Pacific Northwest with the Minneapolis area, while other routes serve the Inland Northwest and Northern Rockies. Wafra and Post Road announced their investment in February 2023 and completed the recapitalization on January 12, 2024 through WRA II-Pioneer (S) LLC and PRSOF II IIG Inc. Future Standard later succeeded Post Road as manager of the digital-infrastructure platform. IIG identified Wafra as its majority shareholder and Future Standard as its other backer in June 2026; current exact ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

companies.name: Mission Clean Energy LLC
companies.subsector: Utility-scale solar and battery storage development
companies.description: Mission Clean Energy LLC is a U.S. utility-scale solar and battery-storage development platform headquartered in San Francisco. Mission develops large projects through subsidiary and project-level entities; approximately 1 GW of Midwest battery projects were described as Mission-owned development assets, while broader multi-gigawatt figures represent the development pipeline rather than operating capacity. Wafra announced the acquisition of a controlling interest in October 2022, and Mission continues to identify an affiliate of Wafra-managed funds as its principal investor. Orsted completed a separate strategic minority investment in December 2024. Exact Wafra and Orsted percentages, Wafra's fund and legal vehicle, and any current founder or API ownership are not publicly disclosed. No platform exit or signed pending platform transfer was identified through the reviewed cutoff.
